market.headline: Opex Friday locks red: SPY -1.10%, QQQ -2.49%; WTI settles at 101.41 as oil crowns a rough tech week
market.note: Official close is in: SPY finished at 763.30 after a 760.64 low, down 1.10% and about 2% on the week. QQQ closed at 709.86, down 2.49% and about 5.5% for the week as chips extended their slide. WTI settled at 101.41 and Brent at 109.86 on Iran tension, which kept the growth selloff alive into the bell. TSLA bounced off 349.33 and closed 354.67. After-hours are quiet. Monday is the Black Monday anniversary and the first real test of whether SPY can reclaim 766.

portfolio.note: TSLL -4.5% and QLD -5.0% led the session. The week is the TSLA stack and QLD sliding with QQQ. Tape is closed for the weekend.

watchlist.note: Official close 763.30 after 760.64 low; -2% on the week
Low 707.23; down about 5.5% for the week
Bounced from 349.33; closed just under Thursday 355.23
Held up better than most chip names again
Low near 703; reports Wed Oct 21 after the close
2x Nasdaq; down about 11% on the week
Worst on the list as AI data-center names get hit
Closed under 100 as risk appetite fades

catalyst.outlook: The close confirmed the morning warning. Hot import prices and strong factory output already trimmed rate-cut hopes before the Oct 27-28 Fed meeting, and WTI settling above 101 on Iran tension added fuel. That mix hit long-duration tech first, which is why QQQ fell more than twice as much as SPY. Next week flips to earnings: Netflix Tuesday, then TSLA and META Wednesday night. If oil cools and those reports hold up, growth can bounce. If oil stays above 100 into Monday, pressure on QQQ and the TSLA stack likely continues.

today.name: Import Prices (Sep)
today.read: Hotter than expected and August was revised down to 0.5%. Fuel imports rose 4.8% and nonfuel 0.7%. Year over year import prices are up 8.1%, the largest gain since July 2022. That kept pressure on yields and growth names like TSLA and QQQ.

today.name: Industrial Production (Sep)
today.read: A clear beat. Manufacturing rose 0.3%, utilities jumped 3.5%, and third-quarter IP ran at a 2.8% annual rate. Growth is holding up despite hot energy costs, which softens the stagflation read from this week's inflation prints.

today.name: Capacity Utilization (Sep)
today.read: Utilization moved up but remains 2.5 points below its long-run average, so factory tightness is not the main inflation driver. Still a mild hawkish tilt alongside hot import prices.

today.name: Monthly options expiration
today.read: Opex did not pin SPY near the big 770 to 772 strikes. It broke below them and sold to a 760.64 low before closing at 763.30. With those positions gone, Monday can move more freely in either direction.

week.name: Cboe extended options hours begin
week.why: Early morning and late sessions start for SPY, QQQ and more. Expect thinner liquidity and wider spreads in those windows.

week.name: NAHB Housing Market Index (Oct)
week.why: Builder mood with mortgage rates above 7%. A read on how rates are biting the housing side of the economy.

week.name: Housing Starts and Building Permits (Sep)
week.why: More housing data. Weak numbers would support the case for easier policy despite hot inflation.

week.name: Netflix earnings (after the close)
week.why: First mega-cap tech report of the season. Sets the tone for growth names into TSLA and META.

week.name: TSLA, META, IBM, LRCX, TXN earnings (after the close)
week.why: The big one for you. TSLA margins, robotaxi and Roadster plans, plus META AI spend and LRCX and TXN reads on the chip slump.

week.name: Initial Jobless Claims
week.why: Claims have hovered near 200K. A jump would be the first crack in the labor market.

week.name: S&P Global Flash PMIs (Oct)
week.why: First look at October activity and price pressures. Watch the prices-paid parts for oil pass-through.

week.name: UMich Sentiment, final (Oct)
week.why: Inflation expectations matter here. Rising expectations would make the Fed's job harder the week before its meeting.

stocks.title: Nasdaq 100 posts its worst week since April 2025
stocks.detail: QQQ finished the week down about 5.5% with over 3 trillion erased from tech in 10 days. Traders blame oil above 100, yields near 5.1%, and AI leverage fears.

stocks.title: Chip stocks extend their longest losing streak since 2010
stocks.detail: SOXX kept sliding on Friday. X points to AI spending doubts and higher borrowing costs, with leveraged chip ETF inflows still pouring in on the dip.

stocks.title: WTI settles at 101.41 as oil pushes stocks lower
stocks.detail: Brent closed near 109.86 on Iran tension and Hormuz shipping risk. Higher oil is the macro story traders keep tying to the QQQ selloff.

stocks.title: VIX jumps about 30% as fear gauges flash extreme
stocks.detail: The VIX spiked from the mid-16s toward 22 before settling near 21, one of its biggest daily moves in months on opex and the oil-driven tech dump.

tech.title: Elorian launches Glimpse, a visual reasoning AI model
tech.detail: The Palo Alto startup, staffed by ex-DeepMind and Apple talent, claims better chart and video reasoning than GPT-6 Astra and opened a research preview today.

tech.title: OpenAI warns staff about spy honeypot recruiting tactics
tech.detail: Internal briefings cover romantic lures and casual approaches after a former engineer was arrested over a hidden recording device. X is full of San Francisco jokes.

tech.title: Terence Tao says math is entering an AI industrial age
tech.detail: After OpenAI dropped hundreds of AI-generated math papers, Tao warned the flood prioritizes volume over insight and could wipe junior research overnight.

tech.title: OpenAI hosts its first DevDay Exchange in Bengaluru
tech.detail: Invite-only Codex sessions and demos ran today with stops planned in Tokyo and Seoul. Developers posted stage shots and Codex mascot swag.

world.title: Norte Fire forces evacuations near San Clemente
world.detail: The fast-moving Orange County blaze grew past 250 acres under Santa Ana winds, with homes burned and orders for San Juan Capistrano and San Clemente zones.

world.title: Trump says oil will drop when Iran ends; prices surge anyway
world.detail: He predicted crude would fall like a rock as the conflict wraps, but Brent settled near 109.86 the same day on Hormuz and tanker risk.

world.title: Iran vows to push US Navy ships farther from its coast
world.detail: Iran says it will force US warships beyond 500 km and reports more tanker incidents near Hormuz. US Central Command says commercial ships still pass.

world.title: Indonesia wildfire haze blankets Southeast Asia
world.detail: Peatland fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan sent toxic smoke into Singapore and Malaysia, with hundreds of thousands of respiratory cases reported.

fact.claim: October is historically the S&P 500's worst month on average.
fact.explain: October has the scary reputation because of the 1929 and 1987 crashes, but its average return is positive. September is the month that has been weakest on average over the long run.

word.definition: Mental calm and steadiness, especially when things are stressful or going against you.
word.example: After a rough week, he met the premarket bounce with equanimity and stuck to his plan.

items.detail: SPY and TSLA are barely drifting after the close. Next week is Netflix Tuesday then TSLA and META Wednesday night. Reclaiming 355 to 363 on TSLA early would help the setup.

items.detail: Sports Desk Noise is +5.34% since the Oct 12 start with a 0% drawdown. Lev200 stays ON and Hold QLD even after today's QLD -5%.

items.detail: Preseason finale at Crypto.com Arena before the Oct 20 opener. Still no confirmed Knecht trade; reports have LA talking Jericho Sims with Milwaukee.

sports.title: Chiefs host Chargers Sunday without Rice
sports.detail: Rashee Rice and LT Josh Simmons are out. L'Jarius Sneed is questionable. KC is about -8.5 at Arrowhead. Against-KC bets still need High confidence and a 5-point edge.

sports.detail: Both are off the injury report. Derwin James, Joe Alt, Tre Harris and Donte Jackson are out. LA is 0-5 and trying to avoid an 0-6 start.

sports.detail: Tip at 10:30 PM ET on ESPN. Regular season opener is Oct 20. Watch for any last roster move before the 15-man cut.

sports.title: Noise +3.32% today; Lev200 still Hold QLD
sports.detail: Paper Noise is 2 up days out of 3 traded, +5.34% since start, 0% drawdown. Lev200 remains ON with QLD Hold despite the Nasdaq slide.
